item.title: Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean Bring The Score To Miami Art Week
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean take their Fugees anniversary into Miami Art Week with a show and an audience-powered exhibit.
item.content:encoded:
Lauryn Hill is turning a Fugees anniversary into a Miami Art Week gathering where the music shares space with listeners’ own stories. She’s joining Wyclef Jean for a December 5 performance at Faena Forum in Miami Beach.

The set anchors The Fourth Space, a new Saint & Citizen event built around the 30th anniversary of The Score. Saint & Citizen’s event announcement pairs their performance with an exhibition tracing Black American and Haitian history, plus a short opening film.

That combination puts the people connected by the record alongside the artists who made it. “The Fourth Space is the one we create through shared culture, memory and experience,” Saint & Citizen CEO Paula Grant said in a statement quoted by Billboard.

The new booking follows Hill and Jean’s launch of the Fugees Hopeline, which invites callers to record personal reflections on hope. The artists’ original project announcement said selected recordings would enter an exhibition curated by Hill with Saint & Citizen.

That project gives listeners something to do beyond requesting their favorite record. Hill’s daughter Selah Marley narrates the phone experience, which also offers messages from the two artists and a new Fugees medley. The recordings are intended to grow into an international audio archive, giving ordinary callers a place in the anniversary alongside the group’s established history.

Hill has made visual work for the anniversary, too, creating three collages that combine archival photographs with typography. The images pull from three decades of the group’s history, extending the celebration beyond the songs people already know by heart.

The pair’s U.S. anniversary performances began November 4 at Berkeley’s Greek Theatre, with announced stops in Las Vegas, Los Angeles and Seattle. Miami adds an art-focused gathering to a celebration that’s already traveled through concert venues.

The organizer’s ticket page lists free exhibition admission from 2-5 P.M. Eastern on December 5, with separate tickets for the evening program. Kaytranada leads the after-party with opening sets from Joe Kay, giving attendees another reason to stay after Hill and Jean leave the stage.

The official ticket listing says the December 5 event is limited to attendees aged 21 and older.

item.title: Keith Sweat Brings Foster-Care Family Drama To Tubi With Fat Joe
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Keith Sweat steps into acting and executive production as Twin Pillars brings separated brothers and Fat Joe to Tubi.
item.content:encoded:
Keith Sweat is putting family separation on television with a new drama that brings Fat Joe into the cast. He’s both an executive producer and an actor in Twin Pillars: A Series, rather than simply lending his name to the credits.

The show’s official announcement identifies Darrin Dewitt Henson as its creator and director, with a November arrival on Tubi. At the center are fraternal twins whose parents’ incarceration sends them into foster care, leaving the brothers to grow into different lives.

Henson plays Dre opposite Alimi Ballard’s Maurice, while Sweat plays a club owner named Snow. Crystal Coney and Sean Anthony Baker also appear alongside Fat Joe.

“Music has always been my way of connecting with people through stories that speak to real-life experiences,” Keith Sweat said in a statement supplied to Billboard. The singer’s explanation places his television work alongside his music, with family and second chances driving this particular project.

Sweat already has a screen-producing credit beyond this new series. His official website lists him as an executive producer of The Secret Between Us, while also promoting the late-night radio program The Sweat Hotel.

Henson brings his own experience with family-centered television, including Soul Food and The Family Business. His career also runs through choreography, with a 2000 MTV Video Music Award for NSYNC’s “Bye Bye Bye” among his credits.

For Hip-Hop listeners, Sweat’s connection to Fat Joe isn’t coming out of nowhere. He’s also appeared on Joe and Jada, where Jadakiss recalled losing money to him during a studio dice game.

The television rollout comes with Sweat still keeping live dates on his calendar. His official schedule lists the Pompano Fall Festival in Deerfield Beach on November 28, followed by December appearances in Nigeria and South Africa.

The first three episodes of Twin Pillars are due on Tubi on November 16.

item.title: Kid Cudi Keeps Weed Off Movie Sets After 20-Blunt Days
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kid Cudi explains how he keeps weed away from work after a rehab stay, drawing a line between downtime and movie sets.
item.content:encoded:
Kid Cudi says movie sets and business meetings now come before marijuana, a change from the days when he estimates he smoked 15 to 20 blunts daily.

His latest account puts a workday boundary on a habit that once followed him everywhere.

During his Big Bro conversation with Travis Barker, released November 11, Cudi explained that his current smoking depends on his schedule.

On days with no obligations, he might smoke about four joints, but work means waiting until he gets home. “I’m not smoking at all during the day,” Cudi said.

His earlier public account also connected marijuana use to acting. In 2025, he described a sober movie performance as different from working while high, saying access to his emotions came more easily when he wasn’t smoking.

“If I was awake, I was smoking no matter what I was doing, right?” Cudi said.

He recalled carrying hundreds of pre-rolls in a Louis Vuitton briefcase, making the next smoke available before the previous one was finished.

His screen credits already included Don’t Look Up and How to Make It in America when he discussed that shift. The question for him wasn’t whether audiences enjoyed his performances, but how he felt while doing the work.

AllHipHop covered his earlier account of seeking help for marijuana use in August 2025, around the release of Cudi: The Memoir and his album Free. His book traced his Cleveland upbringing, music career and experiences with addiction and recovery.

Cudi said treatment changed his habits, though marijuana remains part of his life.

The exchange took place on a show where Cudi usually invites other people to open up. The two also revisited their early connection through Myspace and the MTV period of their careers.

Big Bro launched earlier this year with Kylie Jenner as its first guest, and Barker’s visit brought the host’s own habits into the discussion.

Later in the episode, Cudi said he also smokes cigarettes and wants to become more physically active.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Drake, Nicki Minaj & Lil Wayne Beat ‘Frivolous’ RICO Suit
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Drake, Nicki Minaj and Lil Wayne see a Michigan surveillance case dismissed after a judge finds no basis for the claims.
item.content:encoded:
Drake, Nicki Minaj and Lil Wayne have been dismissed from a Michigan lawsuit accusing Cash Money artists of turning secret surveillance of a woman’s life into music.

A federal judge rejected the allegations as frivolous, ending a case that also named Birdman, Slim and the label.

U.S. District Judge Judith E. Levy issued the dismissal order November 10 in Michigan’s Eastern District. The ruling came during the court’s required review of a complaint filed without prepayment of fees.

Levy wrote: “The Court concludes that Plaintiff’s complaint is frivolous because it lacks an arguable basis in fact or law.” The case was dismissed without prejudice, although Levy also concluded that another amendment would be futile.

Plaintiff Europe R. Colbert, representing herself, accused the defendants of placing surveillance equipment inside her Warren, Michigan home and using private information in recordings.

Those assertions were allegations in her complaint, which the judge rejected, rather than findings that any artist had engaged in surveillance.

Colbert invoked federal racketeering, wiretap and Lanham Act provisions alongside state claims, seeking damages and public corrections. Her amended complaint contained ten causes of action and also named Limp Bizkit among the defendants.

The initial complaint was dated September 28, followed by an amended version in early November.

The judge identified a missing piece of the paperwork behind the music accusations. Colbert referred to an attached list of allegedly infringing recordings, but Levy could not locate it.

Levy wrote: “But there is no Exhibit A attached to the amended complaint, original complaint, or anywhere else on the docket as far as the Court can discern.”

Levy evaluated the allegations under the screening rules for cases brought without upfront court fees. That review allows a judge to dismiss frivolous claims without treating every accusation as established fact.

Cash Money and Birdman also recently secured dismissal from a separate lawsuit over the shooting of Lil Wayne’s tour bus.

That Georgia case concerned a driver’s claims arising from the 2015 attack and was unrelated to Colbert’s Michigan complaint.

Levy additionally denied Colbert permission to appeal without prepaying fees, finding an appeal would not be taken in good faith.

item.title: Skepta Cancels India & Australia Shows To Put Family First
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Skepta steps away from major festival bookings across two countries after saying his family needs to come before the stage.
item.content:encoded:
Skepta is putting his overseas festival run aside for family, pulling out of performances in India and Australia.

The decision removes the London rapper from a stretch of international dates just as his first solo album in seven years reaches listeners.

In his November 11 announcement, the grime veteran said personal circumstances would keep him away from those shows. He described the decision as painful, particularly because the Indian appearance would have been his first performance in the country.

“I hope you understand that I have to put my family first,” Skepta wrote in his statement on X. He did not disclose the private circumstances behind the cancellation.

The message also made clear that Australia already held a special place in his touring history. He told supporters he disliked canceling performances and had been looking forward to returning, while stopping short of announcing replacement dates.

The Australian bookings included Lost Paradise, Beyond The Valley and Wildlands.

Lost Paradise and Beyond The Valley both run from December 28 through January 1, with the former in New South Wales and the latter in Victoria.

Wildlands has Brisbane Showgrounds booked for December 31 before its Perth stop at Arena Joondalup on January 2.

His withdrawal also changes the picture for Rolling Loud India’s second edition. Skepta had been announced alongside Karan Aujla at the top of the second day’s lineup, while Big Sean, Metro Boomin and Burna Boy were booked for the first day.

The announcement arrives less than a week after The Fork and Knife, released November 6 through Big Smoke Records and Epic.

The 15-song project follows 2019’s Ignorance Is Bliss, ending a lengthy gap between his solo full-length records.

Its guests include Project Pat, Asake and Aya Nakamura, with Jme and Frisco also appearing. That new material now reaches listeners without the planned festival appearances in two of the markets on his calendar.

“I’m sorry and I hope to be back with you soon,” Skepta added. His statement offered an apology rather than a new timetable for those performances.

Rolling Loud India’s Mumbai event is scheduled for December 12 and 13.

item.title: Takeoff’s Estate Resolves Sexual Assault Suit Before December Trial
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Takeoff's estate reaches an agreement in the long-running civil case, while attorneys keep the financial details private.
item.content:encoded:
Takeoff‘s estate will not face the December jury trial over a woman’s sexual assault allegations after reaching a resolution in the six-year-old lawsuit. The agreement leaves its financial terms out of public view, with the formal dismissal still to come.

At Thursday’s Los Angeles court appearance, estate attorney Tamar Yeghiayan told Judge Huey P. Cotton, “A dismissal is forthcoming. It will be filed prior to [Dec. 1],” according to Rolling Stone. Cotton replaced the scheduled jury selection with a status hearing.

Attorneys for both sides declined to discuss the terms with the outlet, including whether the agreement involves a payment. That leaves no disclosed settlement amount attached to the resolution.

The case began in August 2020, when a woman identified as Jane Doe sued over an alleged assault at a June house party in Encino. Her complaint included claims of sexual battery, assault, false imprisonment and emotional distress against the Migos rapper.

Takeoff denied the accusations through his attorney Drew Findling. Los Angeles prosecutors declined to pursue criminal charges in April 2021 because of insufficient evidence, but the woman’s civil lawsuit remained in court.

The estate had been fighting to have the complaint thrown out before a jury could hear it. As AllHipHop previously reported, its October request for dismissal centered on text messages the defense said Doe deleted after bringing the case.

That dispute grew out of her October 14 deposition. Lawyers representing the estate argued that the missing messages deprived them of evidence they needed to defend against her allegations, and asked the court to impose sanctions ending the lawsuit.

Doe’s lawyers disputed the defense’s handling of that evidence issue, arguing that they had never received a preservation notice and that the request for the texts came years into the case.

Takeoff’s mother, Titiana Patrice Davenport, became the estate’s administrator through probate proceedings in Georgia. The litigation continued after the rapper was killed in Houston on November 1, 2022, at age 28, shifting the defense of the claim to his estate.

The woman also filed a $6 million creditor claim against the estate, a demand separate from the undisclosed terms of this resolution.

item.title: Young L Mourned By Too $hort As The Pack Loses Its Producer
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Young L's death brings a tribute from Too $hort, who remembers the producer behind The Pack's unmistakable Bay Area sound.
item.content:encoded:
Young L, the rapper and producer who helped shape The Pack’s sound, is being mourned by Too $hort, who announced his death in an Instagram tribute Thursday.

The Bay Area veteran remembered both his music and the group’s reach.

“R.I.P. Young Lloyd. I never heard a Young L beat that didn’t SLAP,” Too $hort wrote in his November 12 post. He also praised The Pack’s influence on other artists.

Too $hort did not disclose a cause of death or say when Young L died.

His message tagged Lil B and Lil Uno, connecting the tribute to the group he helped bring to a wider audience.

Young L was part of the Berkeley lineup alongside Lil B, Lil Uno and Stunnaman. The Pack’s 2006 breakout, “Vans,” brought their sneaker anthem beyond the Bay Area and helped establish the group nationally.

The loss comes weeks after Too $hort revisited how he signed The Pack.

He recalled tracking down the musicians after their friends tried to charge him for an introduction.

That account described a relationship that extended beyond the paperwork. Too $hort took the group on the road and credited them with introducing him to Myspace, while leaving their musical choices in their own hands.

The Pack signed to his Up All Nite imprint with distribution through Jive Records. Young L’s production was central to a group whose members would also build identities outside its original lineup.

By May 2010, “Vans” had sold more than 300,000 copies, according to AllHipHop’s reporting at the time.

That year, The Pack moved into a deal with SMC Recordings and prepared an album called Wolfpack Party.

Too $hort’s recent memories emphasized that the connection had survived those business changes.

He said he remained close with the group and still brought them onstage to perform their breakthrough song.

Too $hort followed his tribute with a second Instagram post captioned “R.I.P. YOUNG L.”

item.title: Beyoncé Makes Cécred Wait Two Years To Meet Her Standards
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Beyoncé puts Cécred through extra testing before its debut, with Tina Knowles revealing why their launch slipped two years.
item.content:encoded:
Beyoncé wasn’t letting Cécred hit shelves just because the team thought it was ready.

Tina Knowles says her daughter’s product demands pushed their intended launch back two years.

In i-D’s newly published interview with Eni Subair, Knowles described repeatedly getting formulas returned. Beyoncé tried them herself, with friends and with her daughters before approving them.

“Then, if one person didn’t have an excellent experience, she would give it back to me,” Knowles told i-D. Knowles had already liked the formulas, but that wasn’t enough to get them past Beyoncé.

Knowles said research and development swallowed considerable money, with testing covering three continents and different hair textures.

The team got frustrated, she recalled, but the products improved.

That history adds context to Beyoncé’s push to reach customers beyond her music audience. She founded and financed Cécred herself, with Knowles serving as vice chairwoman.

Cécred finally arrived in February 2024 with its eight-piece Foundation Collection, covering everything from shampoo and conditioner to treatments and hair oil.

The launch assortment also included a vessel for mixing its fermented rice and rose protein treatment.

The brand’s roots reach back to Headliners, the Houston salon where Knowles worked and Beyoncé spent time as a child. The singer had teased her haircare plans in May 2023, well before customers could buy the finished range.

For the business, that salon connection also became a financial commitment when the range launched. Cécred and BeyGOOD announced a fund with an annual $500,000 allocation for cosmetology scholarships and salon business grants.

The interview arrives after Cécred expanded into Britain’s Space NK stores this autumn.

item.title: Angie Martinez Explains Why Tupac's Unheard Interview Stayed Locked Away
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Angie Martinez brings her guarded Tupac recording to Netflix with guests who revisit the history behind the conversation.
item.content:encoded:
Angie Martinez is ready to share Tupac’s unreleased interview without letting its most heated moments tell the whole story.

Her four-part Netflix project revisits a conversation she kept largely private for three decades.

Martinez told Netflix’s Tudum that releasing everything in 1996 could have damaged relationships and intensified an already dangerous conflict.

Tupac’s death made the decision harder because she didn’t want the recording treated as his final statement.

Martinez explained why she reconsidered keeping the recording private: “I also realized these tapes were bigger than me.”

The series brings in Charlamagne Tha God, Joe Budden, Big Boy, Dream Hampton, RZA and Wallo.

Martinez told Tudum, “The difference now is that I have the opportunity to share them with context.”

She wants the discussion to examine the circumstances around the recording rather than simply circulate its most provocative passages.

That concern has followed the tapes for years, long before Netflix entered the picture.

In a 2017 discussion about releasing the interview, Martinez said she’d tried to contact Tupac’s mother to ask how she wanted it handled.

Afeni Shakur’s death interrupted that effort, leaving Martinez without a settled release plan.

She still intended to make the recording public eventually, but respecting the people connected to it remained part of the decision.

The interview had already become part of Martinez’s own career story through her 2016 memoir, My Voice.

That book also revisited her move from Hot 97 to Power 105.1 and the artist disputes she’d navigated along the way.

Those pages covered more than the stories that made it onto her broadcasts. Martinez also revisited her role mediating artists’ disputes and the decisions that came with interviewing some of rap’s biggest names.

J. Cole supplied the book’s foreword as Martinez put those experiences on the page.

The memoir became a New York Times bestseller, bringing her radio career and recollections to another audience.

By the time of her 2017 Reddit appearance, the unreleased conversation was described as a two-hour recording. Martinez acknowledged the demand to hear it while declining to give a timetable she hadn’t worked out.

The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez arrives on Netflix November 27.

item.title: Snoop Dogg Books Jamie Foxx & Martha Stewart For NBC Christmas Special
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Snoop Dogg lines up a star-packed NBC holiday hangout as Death Row Pictures keeps building its television and film business.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg is turning an NBC hotel-suite party into another television job for himself and a holiday invitation for Jamie Foxx. Martha Stewart’s coming too, joining a guest list that stretches from his music circle to comedy and Broadway.

“Christmas With Snoop” airs December 2 at 10 p.m. on NBC, with Peacock carrying the special the following day, according to Variety.

The setup brings that celebration to television with friends and loved ones gathered in a plush suite for the festivities.

Jane Handcock and October London are among those booked for appearances and musical performances, alongside Foxx and his daughter Anelise. Wayne Brady, Kristin Chenoweth, Adam Devine, Craig Robinson, Nicole Scherzinger and Gwen Stefani also join the lineup.

Snoop’s got a role behind the camera as well, executive producing alongside Sara Ramaker through Death Row Pictures. Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay are executive producers for Jesse Collins Entertainment, bringing another production company into the holiday gathering.

That producer credit connects the special to a bigger piece of Snoop’s business.

His Death Row Pictures signed a multiyear creative partnership with NBCUniversal in 2025 covering film, television, sports entertainment and streaming, giving the relationship room beyond guest appearances.

The company already has his life story headed for theaters, with Jonathan Daviss playing him and Craig Brewer directing.

AllHipHop recently reported that Hercy Miller will portray his father Master P in the movie, which also casts Cynthia Erivo as Afeni Shakur.

The Christmas booking also builds on Snoop’s work across NBC’s biggest entertainment and sports broadcasts. He’s coached on “The Voice” and contributed to Olympic coverage, including Paris in 2024 and Milan-Cortina earlier this year.

His Paris Olympics work earned two Sports Emmys as part of NBCUniversal’s coverage, including the award for Outstanding Live Special – Championship Event.

Those assignments have put the Long Beach rapper in front of audiences far beyond his recording career.

This time, the network’s handing him a holiday special with familiar collaborators while his production company takes a place in the credits.

Universal Pictures has set the Snoop biopic’s upcoming theatrical release for August 6, 2027.
